data.narrative:
Astroscale, a publicly listed Space & Aerospace company founded by Mitsunobu Okada, is examined against a peer universe of 3 same-sector, same-stage public comparables: Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), and Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B). The company has raised $400M+ to date against a current market valuation of $840M.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. The median valuation across the 3 public comps stands at $7.6B, with a range spanning $2.9B to $40.0B. This method anchors the primary valuation signal. A public-comp pricing approach using P/S multiples (sector median: 25.3x across 6 tickers including RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) cannot be applied because Astroscale's revenue figure is not on file.

The analysis supports a triangulated valuation range of $6.4B to $8.7B, centered at a median of $7.6B. This implies a significant upside from the current $840M valuation. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion in peer valuations ($2.9B–$40.0B), which reflects heterogeneity in business model and market position within the Space & Aerospace sector. The single-method reliance also constrains confidence; incorporation of additional revenue or profitability metrics would strengthen the analysis. Astroscale's specific positioning within debris removal should be weighted against broader sector dynamics.
